title: The rank of a lisse sheaf is locally constant
statement: Fix a prime $\ell$ and a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with its $\ell$-adic topology [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and put $E_X=p_X^*\underline E$ [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring, sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients]. Let $L$ be an $E_X$-module sheaf [sk-def-sfb-module-objects] that is lisse: it is locally isomorphic to $E_U^{\oplus n}$, for finite $n\geq0$, on a covering of the small pro-etale site [sk-def-pe-site]. For $r\geq0$, let $X_r\subseteq|X|$ consist of points $x$ such that, for some (equivalently every) object $U\to X$ in a trivializing covering with $x$ in its image, $L|_U$ has rank $r$ near a preimage of $x$. This rank is independent of the trivializing covering and of the preimage. Then the $X_r$ are open and closed, only finitely many are nonempty if $X$ is quasi-compact [def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme], and $X=\coprod_{r\geq0}X_r$, with $L|_{X_r}$ of constant rank $r$. Each $X_r$ is given its open subscheme structure [def-weil-open-immersion].

proof.text: Choose the pro-etale finite-free trivializing cover from [def-sfb-lisse-coefficient-module], with ranks n_i. The cover is fpqc by [sk-def-pe-site]. The actual condensed pullback functor preserves finite biproducts and the regular module: its mapMod part preserves these, and its scalar extension is restriction along the inverse coefficient comparison isomorphism [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients, sk-def-sfb-module-objects]. Its composition isomorphism therefore pulls any rank-n trivialization to a rank-n trivialization on every further scheme. On a nonempty overlap compose the two resulting trivializations and apply [lem-sfb-continuous-coefficient-free-rank], obtaining equal ranks, including rank zero.

source.place: Proof, paragraph 2: locally constant rank and fpqc descent of open subsets; assembled from the two extracted arguments

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-fpqc-labelled-clopen-descent] with labels N and constant functions n_i to obtain closed opens R_r forming a disjoint covering. For any additional trivializing object V of rank a, the overlap comparison in step 1 supplies the hypothesis of the test-morphism clause of that same descent lemma. Thus every preimage v satisfies V.hom(v) in R_r iff a=r. Conversely every x lifts to a member of the original cover, yielding the existential characterization of membership in R_r. This proves both rank characterizations without choosing points on empty overlaps.

source.place: Proof, paragraph 2: locally constant rank and fpqc descent of open subsets; assembled from the two extracted arguments

proof.text: Base change the pro-etale cover to the open subscheme R_r using [lem-galois-fpqc-covering-base-change, sk-def-pe-site]. The rank characterization shows each member labelled n_i different from r is empty. Refine each member with n_i=r by its singleton identity cover, and every other member by the empty cover of its empty scheme. Composition of pro-etale covers gives a cover whose members all carry rank-r trivializations by step 1. This avoids any need to compare different free ranks on an empty scheme. By [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-coproduct-family] and Mathlib nonempty_isColimit_cofanMk_of, the pairwise disjoint open immersions R_r into X give a coproduct cocone, so its Sigma.desc is an isomorphism.

source.place: Proof, paragraph 2: locally constant rank and fpqc descent of open subsets; assembled from the two extracted arguments

proof.text: For a quasi-compact X [def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme], apply the finite-subcover property directly to the covering of X by the rank opens. Any nonempty R_r meets one of the finitely many selected pieces R_a; disjointness forces r=a. Hence the set of nonempty rank opens is contained in a finite set and is finite. The argument also applies to empty X and uses no finiteness of the original trivializing cover.
